items.t: US midterm elections. The first polls close at 00:00 CET, Pennsylvania at 02:00, California at 05:00. [3]
Poland's closed-door national security meeting on a permanent US base; no outcome yet. [4]
Sint-Hubertus: bread blessings across Limburg; Wiemesmeer (Zutendaal) holds its feast today. [5]
AFNORTH **12:30 release** Wed and Thu. Brunssum centre roadworks (Koutenveld, Raadhuisstraat) Wed and Thu. Canes at Nashville, 02:00 CET. [6, 7]
Dutch October inflation flash at 06:30; the Kamer debates the revised tax plan; the Bundestag budget committee takes seven arms purchases. [8, 9, 10]

five.t: **The fridge attacks reached Germany and Portugal**, including two stores in North Rhine-Westphalia. Brussels calls it deliberate, Rome found limited impact at its crisis meeting, and US officials privately suspect Iran for the commissary freezers.
**Russia hit the Ukrainian grid in nine regions on US election day:** 289 drones, 59 cruise and 17 ballistic missiles. Abu Dhabi talks are set for 10–11 Nov.
**Qeshm strikes and talk of a settlement:** Vance “feels really good”, Trump names Pickaxe Mountain as a possible target, and Tehran says Hormuz reopens on day two if Washington moves first.
**US election day, posture options Friday.** NBC reports the options include withdrawing at least 25,000 of about 80,000 US troops in Europe; Poland meets today on a base it would pay for.
**The revised Dutch tax plan drops the defence levy for 2027** and delays the box-3 overhaul to 2029. It still lacks a majority before the 12 Nov vote.

pick.t: If you read one thing: the cold-chain lead. The wave now touches North Rhine-Westphalia and Washington suspects Iran for the commissary hits, so this is a force-protection question as well as a food one.

items.h: Qeshm strikes, and Vance talks of a settlement
items.body: A US official called Monday's strike on Qeshm Island “a defensive measure” against “Iranians using surface to air missiles against US assets”; The Wall Street Journal reported that Washington has carried out “limited strikes” on Iran in recent weeks. [11] Iranian state media reported blasts on Qeshm and at Bandar Lengeh overnight. [12] Vice President JD Vance told CNN: “The president and I both feel really good about the prospect of potentially coming to a negotiated settlement.” Trump told Fox News: “We might have to go after Pickaxe, but that's not a big deal,” naming the Pickaxe Mountain site. [11] Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says “on day two, the Hormuz Strait will reopen” if Washington meets Iran's conditions first; a senior Iranian official told Reuters that “Iran will not submit.” [13, 11]
items.next: Qatari mediators flew to Tehran on Monday night with a draft US–Iran text that has been under negotiation for eight days; no deadline or next round is set. [11] A Chinese special envoy visits Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia in early to mid-November. [14]

items.h: Election-day barrage on the grid; Abu Dhabi talks on 10–11 Nov
items.body: Overnight Russia launched 289 drones and 59 cruise missiles; the Air Force says 257 drones, 49 cruise missiles and 3 ballistic missiles were downed. [15] President Zelensky put the ballistic total at 17 and named power plants and substations in nine regions, from Odesa to Rivne, as the main targets: “It is very telling that all of this happened on the day of the U.S. congressional elections.” [16] Russia's defence ministry says it hit energy sites that supply the army and arms factories; a strike on a city hospital in Kharkiv injured 73. [17] The toll from Monday's bombing of an aid point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, rose to 29, with 48 still missing. [18]
items.next: Envoy Steve Witkoff: “The United States will mediate working-level negotiations between Ukraine and Russia on 10-11 November in Abu Dhabi.” US negotiators meet France, Germany, Britain, the EU and NATO in Brussels this week. [19, 17]

items.h: Midterms: the first polls close at midnight CET
items.body: Republicans go in with narrow majorities in both chambers. [20] Polls close from 00:00 CET Wednesday in parts of Indiana and Kentucky; Pennsylvania at 02:00 CET, California at 05:00. [3] Tracking firms say Russia is posting AI-altered videos on X, including a fabricated claim against Texas Senate nominee James Talarico; Iran has been “relatively quiet”. [21] Polling cited by CNBC puts support for the military action against Iran at 31%. [11]
items.next: Results overnight; Congress returns for the lame-duck session on 9 Nov; the new Congress is seated on 3 Jan 2027. [20, 22]

items.h: Drones hit three more of Sudan's power stations
items.body: Drones on Monday hit the New Halfa and Aroma stations in Kassala state and Al-Ghazali near Merowe, a day after Abu Hamad and Al-Dabbah; Anadolu counts at least 16 stations hit in a week. [23] Sudan filed complaints against Ethiopia at the UN Security Council and the African Union, saying 187 drones in 70 attacks since February came from Ethiopian territory. [24]
items.next: The complaints sit with the UN Security Council and the AU Peace and Security Council; no session date is published. [24]

items.h: North Korea tests cluster warheads during allied drills
items.body: North Korea fired a tactical ballistic missile with a cluster-bomb warhead on 31 Oct and strategic cruise missiles with a cluster warhead on 2 Nov, according to the state agency KCNA, during allied drills. [25, 26] Taiwan's air force runs its Sky Dragon drills 2–6 Nov, and Kinmen held live-fire drills on Tuesday. [27, 28]
items.next: Freedom Flag exercise at Kunsan to 6 Nov; Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders meet in Shenzhen 18–19 Nov. [25, 29]

feature.title: Tehran in its own words: two days, seven conditions
body: Five voices carry Iran's line. Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei has not appeared in public since the war began and speaks through written statements; Maj. Gen. Ahmad Vahidi commands the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). [30] Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf is chief negotiator, Abbas Araghchi is foreign minister, and Esmaeil Baghaei speaks for the ministry. [31, 32]

On 4 Oct Ghalibaf said the strait stays shut until seven conditions from the Islamabad memorandum are met. [31] In an Al Jazeera interview reported on 1 Nov, Araghchi listed them: US recognition of a new Iran–Oman shipping route, sanctions lifted, a smaller US military presence, oil waivers restored, frozen funds released including those in Qatar, all other routes closed, and an end to the war on every front, “especially Israel's attacks on Lebanon”. Under the two-day plan, Washington acts on day one and the strait reopens on day two. [13] Euronews's account of the plan on 2 Nov also lists an end to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports. [32]

On capabilities, the record is mostly claims. Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority requires ships to coordinate with it, and ships that refuse are attacked; the US Treasury says no new oil has loaded at Iranian terminals since 25 Aug. [33] The IRGC navy claims more than 20 operations against US warships, without evidence; the head of US Central Command said in late August that the recognised transit routes were “free of Iranian sea mines”. [34] Vahidi told the Supreme Leader weapons output is up “seven-fold”, a claim not independently verified. [30]
The table sets the dated statements side by side, oldest first.

head: Date

rows: “the Strait of Hormuz will not open until our seven conditions based on the Islamabad memorandum are met” (Al Jazeera) [31]
“Prove your claim of mine-clearing in the Strait of Hormuz with independent evidence, not a statement!” (CBS News) [34]
“any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted response” (Euronews) [30]
“We have upgraded our weaponry, addressed our vulnerabilities, and tested new arms.” (Al Jazeera) [33]
“We have now reached a plan that cuts the implementation time to two days.” (Middle East Eye) [13]
“The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach” (Euronews) [32]

after: IRGC claims about mines, drones and output are unverified.

incidents.when: weekend of 31 Oct – 2 Nov; reported Mon 2 Nov
incidents.place: Germany: Wuppertal and Raesfeld (North Rhine-Westphalia); Reisbach (Bavaria)
incidents.text: Germany's first cases: an Edeka in Reisbach says its cooling was heated to up to 50 °C; a CAP-Markt in Wuppertal reports an “external intervention” and a police complaint. [35] At a Rewe in Raesfeld the Danfoss controls were switched to defrost. [36]

incidents.place: Portugal: seven Intermarché stores (towns not named)
incidents.text: Seven Intermarché stores were hit, reportedly through an outside refrigeration contractor (AFP, as reported by The Hacker News). [37]

incidents.place: Latvia: Krāslava and Ludza (Belarus and Russia borders)
incidents.text: An unidentified drone entered from the east at 18:59; a Blaze interceptor drone went up and self-destructed at 19:19 short of the Russian border. The object left after about 17 minutes. [38]

incidents.place: Italy: Catania and Palermo (Sicily); cases also in Tuscany and Emilia-Romagna
incidents.text: Display-case controllers at three Coop-brand stores in Catania and one in Palermo were reset remotely around 04:00; Italy's National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) found further cases in Tuscany and Emilia-Romagna. [39]

incidents.place: Romania: six stores of one chain (cities not named)
incidents.text: Fridges in six stores heated up overnight. Romania's National Cyber Security Directorate (DNSC) says the controllers sat behind internet-reachable cellular (GSM) routers on old software. [40]

incidents.when: reported 28 Oct; held in Germany for several weeks
incidents.place: Germany: Nuremberg region (planned targets); Romania: Brașov (arson on 14 Sep)
incidents.text: Two Belarusian men are held in Germany on European arrest warrants from a Bucharest court. Romanian prosecutors say they set fire to a defence company in a Brașov industrial park on 14 Sep; security sources told Der Spiegel they planned fires near a railway line and a power transmission route in the Nuremberg region. Romania's intelligence service (SRI) places them in a “Moscow-controlled espionage and sabotage network”. [41]

Police detained a 55-year-old Russian citizen seen photographing trains and rail infrastructure near a level crossing; his devices held “hundreds of thousands” of images of transport sites in Poland and abroad. He is charged with spying for a foreign intelligence service and held for three months. Security services coordinator Tomasz Siemoniak said such activity “has always been accompanied by prior reconnaissance and information gathering.” [42]

leads.title: The fridge wave reaches Germany, and Washington points at Iran
leads.teaser: Two stores in North Rhine-Westphalia and seven in Portugal join the list. Brussels calls it deliberate, Rome reports limited impact after its crisis meeting, and US officials privately suspect Iran for the commissary freezers.
rows: Since the night of 1–2 Nov, stores in at least 11 countries have reported remote tampering with refrigeration: Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Sweden, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Romania, Germany and Portugal, after France on 11–12 Oct. [35, 37, 43] Belgium alone counts about 75 sites. [44]

Attackers switch controllers to defrost or push setpoints to about +50 °C, mostly between 01:00 and 04:00 or over a weekend. [36, 40] Danfoss told NOS the Dutch systems hit were not on a secure network and still used default passwords. [37]

A0 in Europe: no claim, no named suspect; Belgium's federal prosecutor has opened a criminal case. [43] In the US, two people told Defense One that officials suspect Iran-linked hackers of the commissary freezer intrusions, adding that this “could change”. [45]

EU Agriculture Commissioner Christophe Hansen called it a “deliberate attempt to disrupt” the food supply; the Commission is coordinating national cyber-crisis agencies through its liaison network (CyCLONe). [43, 46] The Dutch National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) has issued guidance for owners. [47] Rome's meeting on Tuesday morning, chaired by Undersecretary Alfredo Mantovano with Agriculture Minister Francesco Lollobrigida, the cyber agency and the intelligence chiefs, found “limited impact” in Italy; the postal and communications police are investigating links abroad, and parliament's intelligence committee (Copasir) will ask the government for information. [48]
leads.sw: Baseline requirement 4 (food and water) now has a military mirror: if the commissary hits were Iranian, contracted cold stores serving US and NATO forces are in the same target set. Ask the J4 and the host-nation support cell which contracted cold storage in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany is remote-managed, and who can order it offline at 02:00.

leads.title: Germany hardens its bases; rail sabotage cases surface
leads.teaser: Berlin's top operational commander says US sites have drawn suspected drone surveillance. Two Belarusians held in Germany allegedly planned fires along a Bavarian railway, and Poland charged a Russian who photographed its trains.
rows: Lt. Gen. Alexander Sollfrank, head of the Bundeswehr's Joint Operational Command, said on Sunday that Germany will raise security at military sites and expand counter-drone capability, citing Russian espionage and sabotage and suspected drone surveillance of American bases. [49]
An unidentified drone crossed from the east on Sunday evening; a Blaze interceptor drone went up and self-destructed short of the Russian border. [38]

Two Belarusians held in Germany allegedly planned fires along a railway and a power route near Nuremberg; Poland charged a Russian who photographed its trains at Świdnica. Details are in the incident log. [41, 42]
Day two of the national police readiness order (2–8 Nov); no incident reported. Lithuania has reportedly extended its own Kaliningrad border measures to mid-November. [50]
leads.sw: Germany is the transit hub for any US reinforcement, and both rail cases target the lines a reinforcement would use. Expect tighter base access and counter-drone rules at US installations first, and plan reception, staging and onward movement (RSOM) timelines with slower gates, more escorts and rail-security checks.

pattern: **Same door, more rooms:** 11 countries in two nights, all through internet-reachable controllers with default credentials or old software, some behind cellular routers. The method has not changed since France. [37, 40]
**Night and weekend timing:** hits land between 01:00 and 04:00 or over a weekend, when nobody checks the cold rooms. [40, 51]
**From retail incident to security file:** an EU commissioner calls it deliberate, Italy convenes its intelligence chiefs, and US officials point at Iran for the commissary hits. [39, 45, 46]
**Rail reconnaissance:** two cases in one week, a planned arson along a Bavarian line and a Russian photographer at a Polish crossing, both point at transport networks rather than shops. [41, 42]

hybrid.note: Election interference is still not tracked for Europe: no national election in the area falls soon. For the US vote, warning channels to election officials are at their weakest since 2016; no tampering with voting systems has been reported. [21]

europe.h: Election day: what allies fear from a Republican loss
europe.body: Five NATO diplomats told POLITICO that a Republican defeat could push President Trump toward a harder line: more troops out of Europe, smaller payments into NATO's common funding, limits on the Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) through which allies buy US arms for Kyiv. [52] At least four option sets of force levels and dispositions are due to Hegseth on Friday, with the full review in December; NBC reported that the options include withdrawing at least 25,000 of about 80,000 US personnel in Europe. [53, 54] Congress requires a certification before the number drops below 76,000. [55]
europe.sw: Watch for linkage: a troop decision tied to a Ukraine deal reaches host nations as politics before it reaches them as a planning order.

europe.h: Poland meets today on a permanent US base it would pay for
europe.body: President Karol Nawrocki holds a closed-door national security meeting today on a permanent US base; no outcome had been published by early afternoon. Warsaw would pay $3–4 billion, the base could bring up to 5,000 more permanent troops on top of about 10,000 mostly rotational US troops now in Poland, and Wrocław, Poznań, Bydgoszcz and Szczecin are named as candidate sites. Trump on Truth Social: “If this happens, the location will be announced very soon.” [4] Separately, the Pentagon chose Poland over Germany, the Netherlands and Norway for Europe's first Patriot interceptor maintenance and recertification hub, about $253 million, running in about a year. [56]
europe.sw: A paid-for permanent base in Poland is the posture review's easiest yes. Expect the eastern flank to gain while western sites such as the Benelux garrisons are asked to justify themselves.

euregio.h: A4 resurfacing between Langerwehe and Düren until spring
euregio.body: Work on the A4 toward Aachen started on Monday and runs until spring 2027; two lanes stay open each way, and the Rurscholle rest area closes from Wednesday. [57]
euregio.fy: Allow extra time on the Köln run, including for the Christmas markets.

euregio.h: The Gen Z weekend passed quietly in Aachen and Maastricht
euregio.body: About 2,000 people marched through Aachen on Saturday without notable incidents; two face charges. [58, 59] Maastricht sent 12 people out of the centre and arrested one, while some shops boarded up. [60] The Hague arrested 34, mostly aged 15 to 18. [61]
euregio.sw: Opposition to military-service screening is visible 25 minutes from Brunssum, but the weekend stayed within normal policing.

euregio.h: Brunssum centre roadworks Wednesday and Thursday
euregio.body: Asphalt repairs on 4–5 Nov close parts of Koutenveld and Raadhuisstraat. [7]
euregio.fy: Use the ring roads to reach JFC Brunssum on Wednesday and Thursday.

cards.n: Secretary since early September; Chief of Staff since April; no nominee for either. [62]
Continuing resolution H.R. 6500: FY2026 levels, no new starts or multiyear contracts. [63, 64]
For O-4 and above: House tiered 7–6–5%, Senate flat 3.6%; the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) decides. [65]
Office of Strategic Capital commits up to $450 million to small-drone maker Neros. [66]

words.quote: The president and I both feel really good about the prospect of potentially coming to a negotiated settlement.
words.context: Said hours after the Qeshm strikes; he called the Iranians “unpredictable”, said Trump keeps “kinetic and non-kinetic” options and that no deadline is set. [11]

words.quote: We might have to go after Pickaxe, but that's not a big deal.
words.context: On Pickaxe Mountain, the underground site near Natanz, after calling the Qeshm strikes a “little detour”; he also said “we're not going to allow Iran ever to have a nuclear weapon.” [11]

dod.h: A $450 million loan for small drones, a year before AUTOWARCOM
dod.body: On 2 Nov the Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) signed a conditional loan commitment of up to $450 million with Neros, Inc., a US maker of small dual-use drones; the release page did not load, so terms beyond the headline are not confirmed. [66] The Autonomous Warfare Command (AUTOWARCOM) is still on paper: announced on 30 Sep as a 12th, four-star combatant command “with service-like authorities”, it has a stand-up target of 1 Oct 2027, needs legislation and has no commander. [67, 68, 69] Its Army piece, the three-star Futures and Autonomous Systems Command (FASCOM), stood up on 1 Oct and must field priority autonomous systems by FY2028. [70, 71]
dod.sw: Drone mass is now being bought with loans as well as appropriations, and FASCOM is the Army door into it. Track which FASCOM systems reach V Corps units first; JFC Brunssum's counter-drone and logistics planning will inherit their numbers.

dod.h: Trump is asking how Hegseth and Caine are doing
dod.body: The Atlantic reported on Sunday that Trump has asked allies how Hegseth and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, Gen. Dan Caine, are performing, after what some advisers call “rosy” Iran-war forecasts. The two presented military options to Trump and Vance at the White House the week before; no order to resume large-scale strikes has been given. The White House says Trump has “full confidence” in both men. [72]
dod.sw: The same two men sign off the Europe posture options due on Friday. Doubt at the top tends to speed decisions up, not slow them down.

news.h: Combined Resolve ends Wednesday with Ukrainians scouting for US armour
news.body: At the Joint Multinational Readiness Center in Hohenfels, 1st Armored Brigade, 1st Armored Division trains with more than 3,500 personnel from seven nations, among them about 50 Ukrainian soldiers bringing drone experience from the front; the exercise ends 4 Nov. [73]
news.sw: Ukrainian drone reconnaissance at brigade level is a training input worth pulling into NATO Allied Land Command (LANDCOM) and JFC Brunssum lessons work before FASCOM's own systems arrive.

news.h: Reforger and Neptune Strike wind down; 2027 takes shape
news.body: Resolute Reforger is in its recovery phase in eastern Latvia until 8 Nov, with about 3,000 personnel and 1,000 vehicles under the NATO multinational brigade. [74] Neptune Strike 26-4, with three carrier and amphibious groups from 17 allies in the North Atlantic, ends on 5 Nov. [75] Next on the calendar: Steadfast Dart 27, the Allied Reaction Force deployment to Krivolak in North Macedonia early in 2027, and Quadriga 27 across Germany from March to May. [76, 77]
news.sw: Steadfast Dart and Quadriga both lean on German and Benelux transit; reception-area and host-nation support taskers for JFC Brunssum's staff start this winter.

congress.h: USAREUR-AF's next commander waits on the Senate floor
congress.body: Lt. Gen. Kevin D. Admiral, nominated on 20 Jul to command US Army Europe and Africa and LANDCOM, has sat on the Senate's Executive Calendar since the Armed Services Committee reported him on 23 Sep (PN1188). The post is now a three-star billet; Maj. Gen. Christopher Norrie has performed the duties since Gen. Christopher Donahue stepped down on 2 Jul. [78, 79, 80] Norrie is himself nominated for III Armored Corps. [81] Also pending: Lt. Gen. David Miller Jr. for US Space Command (PN1413, referred on 29 Sep). [82, 83]
congress.sw: The lame duck from 9 Nov is the window for floor votes. Nominations still pending when this Congress adjourns go back to the White House, which would leave USAREUR-AF and LANDCOM under acting leadership into 2027.

congress.h: FY27 defence bill waits for the lame duck
congress.body: The House passed its FY27 NDAA, H.R. 8800, by 216–212 on 22 Jul; the Senate's S. 4784 failed a cloture vote on the motion to proceed, 50–46, on 14 Jul, and there is no conference text. [22, 84] Congress returns the week of 9 Nov. [22] The House bill renews the 76,000-troop floor in Europe and requires an assessment of moving troops to the eastern flank before bringing any home. [85]
congress.sw: The 76,000 floor is the one legal brake on the posture review; it gets settled in conference whatever tonight's result.

items.h: Colonel board recesses Thursday
items.body: The FY27 active-component colonel board (MILPER 26-170) recesses about 5 Nov. [86]
items.fy: Results post on the Army Human Resources Command (HRC) site some weeks later; nothing to do until the release message.

items.h: 2027 pay raise: two numbers on the table
items.body: The House NDAA gives 7% to E-5 and below, 6% to E-6 through O-3 and 5% to O-4 and above; the Senate bill, S. 4784, gives a flat 3.6%, which is also the statutory baseline from the employment cost index. Whichever survives takes effect on 1 Jan 2027. [65, 87]
items.fy: At O-4 and above the gap is 1.4 points of base pay. Budget on 3.6% until a conference text appears.

items.h: Open season starts 9 Nov
items.body: TRICARE Open Season runs 9 Nov to 8 Dec, with changes from 1 Jan; it covers family members' plan choice, not the active-duty member, and no action is needed to keep the current plan. [88] The Federal Benefits Open Season, which includes the Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program (FEDVIP), runs 9 Nov to 14 Dec. [89]
items.fy: Decide whether the family stays on TRICARE Prime overseas or moves to Select, and whether vision cover is worth adding.

dates: TRICARE and Federal Benefits open seasons open
2027 pay raise and benefit changes take effect
career.note: The 2027 housing allowance (BAH), overseas housing (OHA) and cost-of-living (COLA) tables usually publish in mid-December; the IRS has not yet announced the 2027 Thrift Savings Plan (TSP) limits (2026: $24,500, plus $8,000 catch-up). [90, 87]

items.h: Europe's Ukraine force rehearses in Poland from 9 Nov
items.body: Britain and France announced “Koalicja”, the first exercise of the Multinational Force–Ukraine (MNF-U): about 2,800 troops from 10 countries, 1,100 of them French and 300 British, with Belgian, Dutch, German, Estonian, Lithuanian, Polish, Spanish and Swedish contingents, around Nowa Dęba in south-east Poland from 9 to 22 Nov. It is not a NATO operation: no tanks, no offensive mission, and deployment only after a ceasefire. French Gen. Armel Dirou and British Lt Gen. Tom Bateman co-lead it from an operational headquarters in Paris. [91, 92]
items.sw: A reassurance force rehearsing 100 km from Ukraine draws on the same Dutch, Belgian and German units JFC Brunssum plans with. Ask which of them are double-hatted to the NATO Force Model.

items.h: Bundestag committee weighs seven purchases on Wednesday, Eurofighters first
items.body: The budget committee takes seven proposals above €25 million on 4 Nov: a revised Eurofighter production contract (38 Tranche 4, 20 Tranche 5 from 2031, and 15 aircraft refitted for electronic warfare), eight Role 2B field hospitals with an option for 16 more from 2030, SPIKE-ER2 missiles for the H145M, troposcatter radios and training ammunition. No values were published. [10]
items.sw: Role 2B hospitals from 2030 and electronic-warfare Eurofighters from 2031 set the timeline for German medical and air support in regional plans.

items.h: Germany reorders the Patriots it gave Ukraine, but missiles are short
items.body: The federal procurement office (BAAINBw) has ordered two new Patriot fire units to replace the two given to Ukraine in August 2025, after committee approval on 14 Oct, along with containerised maintenance facilities. The defence ministry confirmed a missile shortage in August and says stock transfers are largely exhausted. [93]
items.sw: Launchers return before interceptors do. Air and missile defence cover for reception areas in Germany stays thin into 2027.

items.h: Lithuania fields its first GM200 counter-battery radar
items.body: Lithuania took delivery of its first Thales GM200 MM/C multifunction radar for its new national division; the radar locates artillery positions and tracks first-person-view (FPV) drones. Quantity and value were not disclosed. [94, 95] NATO expects Lithuania to spend 5.33% of GDP on core defence in 2026, the highest in the alliance, one of five allies above the 3.5% guideline. [96]
items.sw: A national division with its own counter-battery and counter-drone radar is a planning asset for the Baltic defence plans JFC Brunssum owns.

items.h: Belgium hands the first of seven minehunters to Bulgaria
items.body: Belgium transferred the Tripartite-class minehunter BNS Bellis (M916) to Bulgaria at Zeebrugge on 3 Nov, where it was renamed Briz before sailing for Burgas. It is the first of seven ships, four of them Belgian, under a Belgian–Dutch–Bulgarian memorandum approved by Bulgaria's parliament on 26 Aug. [97]
items.sw: Benelux mine countermeasures thin out until the new Belgian–Dutch ships arrive.

items.h: A $1.08 billion next Patriot interceptor, and output to triple
items.body: The Army awarded Lockheed Martin $1.08 billion on 2 Nov to develop the PAC-3 Edge “Future Interceptor”: $660.4 million from the government and $423 million of Lockheed's own money. It pairs a new seeker with a Northrop Grumman three-pulse rocket motor, works with the Integrated Battle Command System (IBCS) and the HIMARS Flex launcher, tests from 2027 and is meant to field in 2031. [98] Lockheed delivered 620 PAC-3 MSE missiles in 2025 and plans about 2,000 a year by the end of 2030; a new GEM-T line at Schrobenhausen in Bavaria starts at the end of 2026 with 1,000 missiles on order. [93]
items.sw: Interceptor supply, not launchers, sets how much of the rear area allied air defence can cover. The Schrobenhausen line is the first European GEM-T source worth tracking for host-nation cover.

items.h: Russia scales up anti-jam antennas on its drones
items.body: Defense News reports that Russia's Kometa satellite-navigation anti-jam arrays are in mass use in 16-element form, 20-element arrays are entering serial production, and 32-element antennas have turned up on Shahed-type drones over Kyiv. Ukraine's military intelligence (HUR) says Russian firms ordered more than 100,000 Kometa modules this year, for Geran drones, glide bombs, Iskander-M, Kinzhal and Filin. Ukraine answers by jamming several satellite bands at once and by spoofing. [99]
items.sw: Navigation jamming alone will not stop the next generation of one-way drones. Counter-drone plans for NATO logistics nodes need spoofing and hard kill, not only jammers.

items.h: Rheinmetall adds passive drone detection to Skynex
items.body: Rheinmetall Air Defence will build Silvus (Motorola Solutions) RFeye passive radio-frequency sensors into its Skynex gun system and Skymaster command network, so drones can be detected and located without the system emitting. Skynex fires airburst rounds at 1,000 a minute out to 4 km. No customer or value was given. [100, 101]
items.sw: Passive detection lets a site defend itself without lighting up for Russian electronic intelligence, which matters most at fixed headquarters and depots.

aperture.inject: STARTEX + 3, 02:40. A host-nation contracted cold store holding a corps rear area's blood products and two days of chilled rations reports freezers at +12 °C and rising; its controllers are remote-managed through a cellular router. Stresses baseline requirements 4 (food and water) and 5 (mass casualties). First calls: the contracting officer and the host-nation support cell for an order to disconnect, then the medical logistics officer.

deep.title: “God forbid”: how Moscow tells the hybrid story
body: On Monday Sergei Shoigu, secretary of Russia's Security Council, said Putin has ruled out attacking Europe “three or four times in the past two months”, then added: “God forbid you live to see a day when Russia launches a hybrid war against you.” [102]

Heard from Moscow, the line does three jobs. It denies, keeping every incident below the level of a collective response. It threatens, implying that what Europe sees is not yet the real thing. And it recasts Polish police readiness and German base hardening as hysteria; a public told its alarm is overblown is slower to pay for resilience. Shoigu spoke the day before Washington's suspicion of Iran for the commissary hits became public. [45]

items.h: Tesla runs unsupervised robotaxi rides in Fort Worth
items.body: Tesla's Robotaxi service began fully unsupervised public rides in Fort Worth, Texas, at 06:00 local time on 2 Nov, with no safety monitor on board, using Model Y cars across about 143 square miles. Fort Worth is the seventh unsupervised city after Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando and Tampa; fleet size and fares were not published. [103]

items.h: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5: 1.6 trillion parameters, 48 billion active
items.body: Meituan released LongCat-2.5 on 2 Nov, a multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 1.6 trillion total parameters and about 48 billion active per token, built for long agent runs over whole codebases. It is live in Meituan's chat service and API; open weights on GitHub and Hugging Face are promised but not yet out, and no benchmarks, context length or prices were published. [104]

items.h: Agility's Digit passes 100,000 totes at a GXO warehouse
items.body: Agility Robotics said on 2 Nov that its Digit humanoid has moved more than 100,000 totes at GXO's Georgia site since June 2024, a company figure; GXO signed for two more US sites, in Statesville, North Carolina and Lebanon, Tennessee, starting in early 2027. No unit counts were given. [105]

items.h: Revised tax plan: no defence levy in 2027, box 3 slips to 2029
items.body: The cabinet sent the amended 2027 tax plan to the Kamer today. It scraps the vrijheidsbijdrage, an extra tax on labour meant to raise €347 million for defence in 2027, to be replaced by cuts to tax benefits still to be agreed; moves the new box-3 tax on investment gains from 2028 to 2029, partly paid from a €3.1 billion reserve; and drops the rise in VAT on flowers and plants from 9% to 21% in 2028. [9]
items.fy: The line that reaches your wallet is fuel: the planned fuel-duty increase is out of the revised plan. [9]

items.h: Still no majority for Wednesday's debate
items.body: The debate is Wednesday and the vote Thursday 12 Nov. In the Tweede Kamer, ChristenUnie, 50Plus and Groep Markuszower could just about carry it; in the Eerste Kamer the cabinet still needs opposition votes from the left or the right. [9] Pro and Volt have walked away; JA21, SGP and BBB want commitments on asylum, nitrogen, abortion and surrogacy. [118]
items.fy: If the plan falls, the fuel-duty discount falls with it. [118]

otd.title: On this day · 3 November 1944
otd.body: The 112th Infantry of the US 28th Infantry Division crossed the Kall gorge and took Schmidt, about 40 km from Heerlen, the deepest point of the first Hürtgen attack. A single logging trail and a bridge over the Kall served as both attack route and supply line, and nobody had sent a patrol down it first. German counterattacks drove the regiment back across the Kall by 8 Nov; the division lost 6,184 men in the battle. Source: David T. Zabecki, HistoryNet. [136]

culture.title: Sint-Hubertus, today
culture.body: Hubert, patron saint of hunters since the 11th century, has his feast on 3 November. Across Belgian and Dutch Limburg, priests bless bread rolls (“hubkes”), once eaten as protection against rabies, along with horses and dogs. In Wiemesmeer (Zutendaal), about 35 minutes away, the feast has been held on 3 November every year since 1947, with hunting horns and an animal blessing. [5]
